# 1 Samuel Chapter 31 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 168r–168v | **Source Image:** 1SA_031_page_001.jpg, 1SA_031_page_002.jpg

---

**1** Now the Philistines were fighting against Israel, and the men of Israel fled before the Philistines and fell slain on Mount Gilboa.
**2** And the Philistines overtook Saul and his sons, and the Philistines struck down Jonathan and Abinadab and Malchi-shua, the sons of Saul.
**3** The battle pressed hard against Saul, and the archers found him, and he was severely wounded by the archers.
**4** Then Saul said to his armor-bearer, "Draw your sword and thrust me through with it, lest these uncircumcised come and thrust me through and deal shamefully with me." But his armor-bearer would not, for he was greatly afraid. So Saul took the sword and fell upon it.
**5** And when his armor-bearer saw that Saul was dead, he also fell upon his sword and died with him.
**6** So Saul died, and his three sons, and his armor-bearer, and all his men, on that same day together.
**7** And when the men of Israel who were on the other side of the valley and those beyond the Jordan saw that the men of Israel had fled and that Saul and his sons were dead, they abandoned their cities and fled. And the Philistines came and dwelt in them.
**8** On the next day, when the Philistines came to strip the slain, they found Saul and his three sons fallen on Mount Gilboa.
**9** And they cut off his head and stripped off his armor, and sent messengers throughout the land of the Philistines, to carry the good news to the house of their idols and to the people.
**10** They put his armor in the temple of Ashtaroth, and they fastened his body to the wall of Beth-shan.
**11** But when the inhabitants of Jabesh-gilead heard what the Philistines had done to Saul,
**12** all the valiant men arose and walked all night and took the body of Saul and the bodies of his sons from the wall of Beth-shan, and they came to Jabesh and burned them there.
**13** And they took their bones and buried them under the tamarisk tree in Jabesh, and fasted seven days.

---
## SOPHIA's Council Notes

All three translators agreed on the verse count (13 verses) and narrative structure for this chapter. SOPHIA follows the LOGOS formal-equivalence rendering as the baseline consensus, adopting PNEUMA's phrasing where it demonstrably improves clarity without sacrificing accuracy. Key terms and theological vocabulary were consistently rendered across all three translations.

---
## ⚠️ Disagreement Log

### Verse 1
- **EMET:** "And-[the]-Philistines [were]-fighting against-Israel, and-fled [the]-men of-Israel from-before [the]-Philistines, and-fell slain on-Mount Gilboa."
- **LOGOS:** "Now the Philistines were fighting against Israel, and the men of Israel fled before the Philistines and fell slain on Mount Gilboa."
- **PNEUMA:** "The Philistines attacked Israel, and the Israelites fled before them. Many fell dead on Mount Gilboa."
- **Resolution:** SOPHIA follows the LOGOS rendering as the formal-equivalence baseline, noting PNEUMA's dynamic phrasing as a valid alternative reading.
### Verse 2
- **EMET:** "And-overtook [the]-Philistines Saul and-his-sons, and-struck [the]-Philistines Jonathan and-Abinadab and-Malchi-shua, sons of-Saul."
- **LOGOS:** "And the Philistines overtook Saul and his sons, and the Philistines struck down Jonathan and Abinadab and Malchi-shua, the sons of Saul."
- **PNEUMA:** "The Philistines pressed hard after Saul and his sons, and they killed Jonathan, Abinadab, and Malchi-shua — Saul's sons."
- **Resolution:** SOPHIA follows the LOGOS rendering as the formal-equivalence baseline, noting PNEUMA's dynamic phrasing as a valid alternative reading.
### Verse 3

- **LOGOS:** "The battle pressed hard against Saul, and the archers found him, and he was severely wounded by the archers."
- **PNEUMA:** "The fighting grew fierce around Saul. The archers found him, and he was critically wounded."
- **Resolution:** SOPHIA follows the LOGOS rendering as the formal-equivalence baseline, noting PNEUMA's dynamic phrasing as a valid alternative reading.

- **LOGOS:** "And they cut off his head and stripped off his armor, and sent messengers throughout the land of the Philistines, to carry the good news to the house ..."

- **Resolution:** SOPHIA follows the LOGOS rendering as the formal-equivalence baseline, noting PNEUMA's dynamic phrasing as a valid alternative reading.
### Verse 12
